newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut bourse ends week on downward note.
newsitem.headline: Beirut bourse ends week on downward note.

text.p: Most shares retreated on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ending on Friday but dealers said a period of consolidation was healthy for the market.
The LIBX bank index fell 4.90 percent to 190.04. The LISPI general index fell 1.11 percent to 96.26 and the BLOM general index fell 1.95 percent to 1091.33.
"This created a realistic atmosphere. It gave people a dose of reality. Markets do go down. It is not a big deal," Alain Balian, deputy manager at Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest said.
Market turnover fell 29.6 percent to 1,098,778 shares from 1,424,526 a week earlier for a value of $13,568,706 against $15,516,438.
Solidere shares, regarded by most bankers as the most undervalued stocks on the market, fell despite heavy demand.
Solidere A shares fell 2.97 percent to $12.625 from $13 and B shares fell 0.97 percent to $12.875 from $13.
On the London Stock Exchange, Solidere's global depositary receipts rose 2.5 percent to $17.325 on Friday from $16.9 a week earlier.
Banque Audi dropped 2.75 percent to $27.25 from $28 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell 4.8 percent to $20.75 from $21.75. BOB fell 7.95 percent to $5.5 from $5.9375 a week earlier.
"It is a period of consolidation. People are getting ready for second half of year results. Some are taking profits," Balian said.
Supply outstripped demand for all three bank shares.
"I think bank shares will eventually go up because there are no other investment options in Lebanon," he added.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was steady at $1.2813. Pipemaker Eternit rose to $1.9063 from $1.78125 in June when it was last traded.
There was no trade in tilemaker Uniceramic or Ciments Blancs.
